lessons: Hook lines that directly state a surprising consequence or unusual fact (e.g., Tuna meat vs. Cod, Shark living for centuries) achieve higher start benchmarks (0.52 to 0.57 vs_similar_start) and keep retention above 1.8 at 10%.
Abstract or overly broad premise lines at the very start cause immediate drop-offs; specific physiological contrasts retain attention better.

Lines that transition into heavy scientific explanations or mechanism breakdowns (e.g., bromelain enzymes or water chemistry) trigger the largest single-point drop-offs, often losing 20% to 36% of viewers around 7% to 14% into the video.

Videos with exceptional retention at the end (like the Greenland shark, keeping 1.10 at the end) maintain high viewer engagement throughout by continuously posing structural mysteries rather than settling into dry exposition.
worst_moment_types: Introducing complex scientific terms or definitions too early in the video (e.g., bromelain, cellular room separation).
Providing slow, methodical explanations of physical processes (e.g., boiling off sap or how dead skin cells absorb water) rather than immediate narrative progression.
best_hook_types: Direct comparative hooks contrasting two familiar items with surprising differences (e.g., Tuna vs. Cod).
Extreme superlative or temporal claims (e.g., sharks older than the United States, foods that last forever).
